# Purpose

Award credit for a defensible global free-body diagram, correct smooth-contact boundary condition, explicit global and local sign conventions, correct local internal resultants, valid rectangular-section properties, axial-plus-bending stress superposition, a correct beam-shear calculation at point A, and an appropriately limited engineering assessment.

# Scope of the Base Problem

The base model assumes static loading, a straight prismatic rectangular member, a concentrated technician load at G, small deformation, and linear-elastic nominal-stress formulas. Support B supplies horizontal and vertical reactions; C is smooth against a vertical wall and therefore supplies only a horizontal reaction. The model excludes member self-weight, local bearing and contact stress, connection behavior, lateral instability, technician motion, impact, vibration, fatigue, material nonlinearity, and regulatory access-system design.

Point A is assigned the coordinate y_A above the centroidal neutral axis. Instructors may change y_A in the Builder while keeping |y_A| <= t/2.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation and load path: 20%;
- student idealization, boundary conditions, and assumptions: 20%;
- reactions and local internal resultants: 25%;
- section properties and stress calculations: 25%;
- stress element, assessment, and limitations: 10%.
